title: What Is Salary Packaging Australia? Your Guide to Hourly to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Discover what is salary packaging Australia and how it differs from casual loading and super. Convert hourly to annual pay using Fair Work and ATO figures, including tax brackets a
salarySummary: For a casual employee on a $30 base hourly rate working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay including 25% casual loading is $74,100 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between casual loading and salary packaging?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of your base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. Salary packaging (also called salary sacrificing) is an arrangement where you forgo part of your salary in exchange for benefits like a car or super contributions. They are separate concepts: casual loading is mandatory for casual employees under awards, while salary packaging is voluntary and subject to employer agreement and FBT rules.

faqs.q: How is super calculated for casual employees?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, which includes your base rate plus any casual loading. For example, if your base rate is $26.44 and you receive 25% casual loading ($33.05), super is 12% of $33.05 per hour. Super is paid on top of your gross pay, not deducted from it, and is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

faqs.q: What tax will I pay on my annual salary?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy of 2% applies (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). These are estimates; your actual tax may vary due to offsets, HELP repayments, or salary packaging.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Whether you're negotiating a salary or checking a job offer, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual pay is essential. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, and the formula is straightforward: **annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

For casual employees, a 25% casual loading is typically added to the base rate. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and check a box to include casual loading. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour** for permanent employees, or **$33.05 per hour** for casuals including the 25% loading. This works out to **$1,004.90 per week** for a 38-hour week (permanent) or **$1,256.13 per week** (casual). Many employees are covered by industry or occupation awards that set higher minimum rates. Always check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Casual loading compensates for not receiving paid leave (annual, sick, personal). It is **not** part of your base rate – it's an additional 25% on top. Superannuation guarantee (currently 12%) is calculated on your ordinary time earnings, which for casuals includes the casual loading. So if your base rate is $30, your casual rate is $37.50, and super is 12% of $37.50 – paid on top of your gross pay. The super guarantee is capped at a maximum contribution base of **$270,830 per year**.

### Fortnightly Pay and Annual Estimates

Most employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For a permanent employee on the minimum wage: $1,004.90 × 2 = **$2,009.80 per fortnight**. For a casual on the minimum wage: $1,256.13 × 2 = **$2,512.26 per fortnight**. Annual gross pay is hourly × hours per week × 52. For a permanent minimum wage earner: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,254.88**. For a casual: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = **$65,306.80**.

### Average Earnings vs. Your Pay

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for May 2026. Full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged **$2,083.70 per week** (or about **$108,352 annually**). All employees (including part-time) averaged **$1,579.20 per week**. These are **averages**, not medians for any specific job. Your pay may be higher or lower depending on your industry, experience, and award.

### Tax on Your Annual Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy of 2% applies (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not confirmed). These rates assume you claim the full tax-free threshold. No HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging deductions are included in this estimate.

### What Is Salary Packaging Australia?

**What is salary packaging Australia?** It's an arrangement where you sacrifice part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits such as a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. Salary packaging can reduce your taxable income, but it is **not** included in the simple hourly-to-annual estimate on this site. If you use salary packaging, your take-home pay will differ from the figures shown here. Always consult a tax professional or your employer for personalised advice.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Resources

To estimate your own annual pay, use [the timesheet](/) on this site. Enter your base hourly rate, select casual loading if applicable, and see your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay. For more detailed information, refer to:
- [Super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) – explains super guarantee and salary sacrifice.
- [Casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) – details on when and how casual loading applies.
- [Minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) – current rates and award coverage.
- [Take-home pay](/topics/take-home) – after-tax estimates using the latest tax brackets.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Final Thoughts

Understanding your hourly to annual conversion helps you compare job offers, budget, and plan for tax. Remember that casual loading and super are paid on top of your base rate, and salary packaging is a separate option that can affect your net income. Use the tools and guides on this site to get a clearer picture of your earnings.
